one_liner: Research demo that fuses bit-unpacking and dictionary lookup with AVX2/AVX-512 gathers; about 2x its own scalar decoder.
what_it_does: Dictionary-codes an array of 64-bit values: builds a dictionary of distinct values, replaces each value by its index, and bit-packs the indexes. Decoding goes through codec classes (SimpleDictCODEC, AVXDictCODEC, AVX512DictCODEC) whose compress() returns a dictionary_coded_t struct and whose uncompress/fastuncompress/fastrangeuncompress write uint64_t values into a caller-supplied buffer. It is a header-only prototype with its own format, not a drop-in for any existing columnar or codec API.
how_it_is_fast: The fast path never materializes the index array: one generated, fully unrolled routine per bit width (0-32) loads 256 (AVX2) or 512 (AVX-512) packed indexes with vector loads, isolates each lane with shifts and masks, and feeds the 32-bit indexes straight into vpgatherdq (_mm256_i32gather_epi64 / _mm512_i32gather_epi64) to fetch the 64-bit dictionary words, which are stored directly to the output. The scalar baseline instead unpacks to a temporary uint32 buffer and then does a separate lookup loop. A blocked variant (fastrangeuncompress) decodes into a cache-sized buffer to avoid RAM round trips.
when_to_use: Decoding long arrays of 64-bit values (or pointers) with few distinct values, such as Parquet- or ORC-style dictionary-encoded columns, on x86-64 with fast gathers (Skylake or later, AVX-512 parts).
Small to medium dictionaries that stay in L1/L2: on Skylake the AVX2 path is about 1.9-2.1 cycles per value against about 4.0-4.1 for the scalar unpack-then-lookup loop up to 4096 entries.
As a reference design when adding a fused unpack+gather decode kernel to your own column store; the per-bit-width kernels are generated code that can be lifted.
Block-wise decoding into a cache-resident buffer (fastrangeuncompress), which on Skylake reached about 1.15-1.3 cycles per value for small dictionaries.
when_not_to_use: Production use: the README says it is a demo, uses its own format, and is not meant to plug into an existing framework.

Untrusted compressed input: there are no bounds checks; any index at or above dictionary_size makes the gather read outside the dictionary array, and length/alignment preconditions are only assert()s.
Large dictionaries that spill out of cache: the gain shrinks to 11.85 vs 8.47 cycles per value at 1,048,576 entries on Skylake and 21.93 vs 16.33 (AVX2) on Knights Landing.
Non-x86 targets or CPUs without AVX2 (the headers #error out), or older Haswell/Broadwell parts where the README warns vpgather was slow.
Arrays whose length is not a multiple of 256 (AVX2) or 512 (AVX-512), arrays over 2^32 values (uint32 counts), or value types other than 64-bit words.

integration.min_toolchain: C++11; Makefile builds with -O3 -march=native; README results from GCC 5.3.0
integration.platforms: x86-64 only: AVX2 required for the fast path, AVX-512F for the AVX-512 codec; scalar codec is portable C++ but uses __builtin_clz (GCC/Clang)
integration.thread_safety: Codec objects hold a temporary buffer and are documented as not thread-safe (one instance per thread); the static fastuncompress/fastrangeuncompress functions keep no state.

gotchas: dictionary_coded_t has a move constructor taking const&& that copies the raw dictionary/compressed_data pointers without nulling the source, so any real move (std::move, or a compiler that skips NRVO in compress()) leads to a double delete[]; the code relies on copy elision.

bit_width is computed as 32 - __builtin_clz(dictionary_size), so power-of-two dictionaries (every size in the benchmark) use one more bit than needed (2 entries are packed at 2 bits), and an empty input calls __builtin_clz(0), which is undefined.
The scalar (32-value blocks), AVX2 (256-value) and AVX-512 (512-value) codecs write different packed layouts; data compressed by one cannot be decoded by another.

avxunpackdict, avxpack, avxunpack and the bpacking.h routines are non-inline, non-static functions defined in headers, so including the headers from two translation units gives multiple-definition link errors; the Makefile's test target covers only the scalar and AVX2 codecs (AVX-512 is exercised only by asserts inside the benchmark).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: simdcomp, FastPFor and TurboPFor decode packed integers but leave the dictionary lookup to you; pick this when the end product is 64-bit dictionary values and you want the unpack and lookup fused in one pass, accepting a prototype. For a maintained bit-unpacking library in a real system, Apache ORC's AVX-512 RLE unpacking or simdcomp is the safer base.
verified_claims_summary: The repo's decodebenchmark (8,388,608 uniformly random indexes, best of 5 runs timed with rdtsc, i.e. TSC ticks) shows AVX2 fused decode at 1.91 cycles per value against 4.00 for the repo's own scalar unpack-then-lookup decoder on Skylake with GCC 5.3.0 for a 2-entry dictionary, 2.12 vs 4.14 at 4096 entries and 8.47 vs 11.85 at 1,048,576. On an unnamed Knights Landing part, AVX-512 reached 1.48 cycles per value against 3.22 (AVX2) and 7.75 (scalar) at size 2. No external codec was measured.
status_note: Abandoned since April 2017 (25 commits, no issues filed) but Apache-2.0 and header-only; treat it as a reference kernel to copy and harden, not a dependency.
